📌 [...] Hello, Product Hunt 🙌🏻 I'm Daniil, a software engineer. Today I'm launching \\Burrow\\: free, open-source virtual machines for Apple silicon Macs. \\🧩 Why I built it\\ I needed Linux, Windows and a clean macOS on my Mac, and I didn't want to pay for a Parallels license. So I built the tool I wanted: click \\+\\, pick a system, done. \\📦 What is Burrow?\\ A native SwiftUI app built on Apple's Virtualization.framework, plus `burrowctl`, a CLI for running the same machines headless. Everything runs locally, it's MIT licensed, and there's no account. \\🔑 Key features\\ - \\No ISO hunting:\\ Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian and Alpine are downloaded straight from each publisher and verified against SHA-256 - \\Windows 11 on ARM:\\ Setup runs unattended, with no TPM or Secure Boot checks and a local [...] unattended, with no TPM or Secure Boot checks and a local account; drivers install automatically \\⚙️ Under the hood\\ Linux and macOS run on Virtualization.framework. Windows runs on QEMU with Hypervisor.framework, because the Windows boot manager hangs under Virtualization.framework. I also patched QEMU for a 60 fps display. \\🚧 Honest limitations\\ ARM64 guests only. Windows has no vTPM or 3D acceleration yet, and there's no USB passthrough. PRs are very welcome; these are great first contributions. \\🙏 Your feedback\\ What would make you drop Parallels or UTM for this? Bug reports, feature requests and ⭐ on GitHub all help a lot. 👉  Best, Daniil

Want Ubuntu, Windows 11 or a fresh copy of macOS on your Mac? Open Burrow, click +, pick a system and click Download & Create. Burrow fetches the installer from the publisher, checks it, builds the machine and starts setup. That's it. [...] |
|  |
| No ISO hunting | The latest Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian and Alpine come straight from each publisher, checked against the published SHA-256. Images are cached for reuse. |
| Windows 11 on ARM | Pick a language on Microsoft's own download page and click Download; Burrow fetches the drivers, creates the machine and runs Setup unattended. |
| macOS guests | Downloads the newest macOS your Mac supports (or uses a local IPSW) and installs it, with progress in the sidebar. |
| Suspend & resume | Saves memory and device state to disk and continues exactly where you left off. |
| Instant clones & snapshots | APFS copy-on-write: no waiting, and no extra space until the guest writes new data. | [...] Burrow is a native SwiftUI app built on Apple's Virtualization.framework, plus `burrowctl`, a command-line tool for running the same machines headless in scripts and on servers. Everything runs locally, and the code is MIT licensed.

Note

Burrow is an original implementation. Parallels Desktop was studied only at the architecture level (which components exist and which system frameworks they use); no code was copied or translated.

## Quick start

### Requirements

 Apple silicon Mac (M1 or newer) on macOS 14 Sonoma or later
 Xcode with Swift 6 to build from source
 For Windows 11 guests: QEMU (`brew install qemu`)

### Build and run

```
cd# → build/Burrow.app and build/burrowctl #
```

If you installed via Homebrew, a `burrow` shim is on your PATH, so you can use `command: "burrow", args: ["mcp"]` instead of the bundle path. Reload the agent and ask in plain language.

Windows preview builds include the stdio bridge in source under `windows/Tools/McpStdioBridge/` and in release artifacts as `Assets\Mcp\burrow-mcp-stdio.exe`. [...] Burrow puts everything your Mac needs in one free, native app: junk cleanup, dev-artifact purge, app uninstall with leftover removal, duplicate finding, safe maintenance, disk maps, and live system status — powered by one bundled engine binary (burrow-engine, FSL-1.1 — see Attribution) whose commands mirror Mole's `mo`, so there's nothing else to install. It keeps months of local metric history and runs a built-in MCP server, so AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can watch, query, and care for your Mac — actions are consent-gated and audited, and Trash-based removals remain recoverable until the Trash is emptied. Permanent deletion requires separate consent and cannot be undone. Native on macOS, with a Windows preview under `windows/`.

Mac: [...] Burrow lives in the menu bar (it's a menu-bar agent). Click the icon → Open Burrow — or turn the menu-bar icon off in Settings to run it as a Dock app. If a macOS build freezes while Burrow creates that status item, the next launch stays in Dock-based compatibility mode on the same OS build and offers a one-click redacted diagnostic report. Automatic Sparkle startup waits until the initial AppKit launch turn has settled and the status item is stable; if the updater then fails its own stability window, later automatic checks pause for that app/OS build while manual checks remain available. A new macOS build retries a guarded status item; a new Burrow or macOS build retries an updater that previously failed its stability window.
